results.title: Northflank vs Heroku: which platform fits your applications and team? | Blog — Northflank
highlights:
- Heroku: There is no free dyno tier. Personal-account Eco costs $5 per month for a shared pool of 1,000 dyno hours and sleeps after 30 minutes of inactivity. Basic is prorated up to $7 per dyno monthly; Standard-1X up to $25. Data services, add-ons, CI, and Private or Shield resources add costs. Review Apps and one-off dynos consume normal resources. Heroku operates the runtime.
- Northflank Cloud: The free, always-on Sandbox includes two services, one database, and two cron jobs. Pay-as-you-go has no seat fees, meters resources by the second, and currently lists $0.01667 per vCPU-hour, $0.00833 per GB-hour, $0.15 per GB-month of SSD storage, and $0.06 per GB of egress. Enterprise pricing is custom and can include commitments, SLAs, 24/7 support, and onboarding.
- Northflank BYOC: Your cloud provider bills the underlying infrastructure directly, while Northflank currently charges $0.01389 per vCPU-hour, $0.00139 per GB-hour, and $0.00278 per GB of GPU VRAM-hour. Direct billing preserves applicable cloud credits, reservations, commitments, negotiated rates, and customer capacity choices. Include minimum cluster capacity and retained cloud-account responsibilities in the total cost.
- Total cost: Model workloads, data, builds, previews, transfer, support, cluster minimums, and engineering time. Northflank may reduce cost when granular allocation, spot capacity, or direct billing outweigh retained responsibility. For Heroku, include dyno, data-service, add-on, Private Space, and applicable contract charges in the total-cost calculation.

results.title: Which platform is best for running AI-generated code securely at scale? | Blog — Northflank
highlights:
- Isolation: Northflank sandboxes support hardware-virtualized microVM approaches such as Kata Containers and Firecracker, plus gVisor user-space-kernel isolation. The runtime depends on the workload and infrastructure; Northflank Cloud GPU workloads use gVisor by default.
- Execution interfaces: Deploy OCI images and manage sandboxes through the Northflank dashboard, REST API, CLI, or JavaScript client.
- Lifecycle and storage: Sandboxes have no platform-imposed session-duration limit. Use ephemeral storage or attach a persistent volume. Scaling to zero stops compute billing while the configuration and volume remain.
- Networking: Expose public or private ports. On BYOC clusters, Network Policies can restrict ingress and egress by workload, project, IP/CIDR, or FQDN.
- Full-stack infrastructure: Run services, jobs, databases, storage, and GPU workloads around the sandbox on the same platform.
- Work from your AI coding tool: If you use a compatible coding agent, install Northflank Skills to give it Northflank-specific guidance for deploying, operating, and automating sandbox workloads and the surrounding application stack through the CLI or API.
- Security and governance: Apply secret injection, scoped API roles, SAML or OIDC SSO, RBAC, and platform audit logs.
- Production scale: Northflank has operated millions of microVMs each month since 2021 across startups, public companies, and government deployments. In the ComputeSDK 2026 Scale Invitational, Northflank also reached 100,000 concurrent live sandboxes from a cold start in 24 seconds with zero failures.
- Pricing: Northflank Cloud bills per second at $0.01667 per vCPU-hour and $0.00833 per GB-hour. With self-serve BYOC, you pay your cloud provider directly, retain your cloud credits and existing billing relationships, and Northflank charges $0.01389 per vCPU-hour, $0.00139 per GB-hour, and $0.00278 per GB of GPU VRAM per hour. For a provider-by-provider view, the AI sandbox pricing comparison compares PaaS rates, billing models, GPU pricing, and BYOC costs at scale.
- Infrastructure placement: Deploy on Northflank Cloud, use BYOC sandbox clusters for workloads in your cloud account, or use BYOK for a compatible Kubernetes cluster.
- Compliance: Northflank is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant and HIPAA compliant, with BAAs supported under Enterprise contracts. Platform compliance does not make your application compliant.

# Best platforms for high concurrency sandbox environments in 2026

### 1. Northflank

Northflank provides isolated sandbox environments for AI agents and code execution, with fast startup and support for thousands of concurrent sessions. Run coding agents, generated APIs, scripts, repository builds, and GPU tasks in custom container environments, with persistent volumes when files need to survive between runs.

Northflank combines API-driven sandbox provisioning with horizontal scaling and workload scheduling to support parallel execution. Create separate environments for users or tasks, configure compute and networking, and run ephemeral or persistent sandboxes on Northflank Cloud or your own infrastructure.

...

- Concurrent sandbox execution: Run thousands of isolated environments for parallel agent tasks, code evaluation, and multi-tenant workloads.
- Horizontal autoscaling: Configure minimum and maximum deployment instance counts and scaling thresholds for CPU, memory, or requests per second. Create distinct per-task sandboxes through the API when each agent needs its own environment.
- Workload scheduling: Bin-packing places workloads across available compute to improve resource utilization while maintaining their isolation boundaries.
- Fast startup: Sub-second sandbox boot times on Northflank Cloud for quickly provisioning execution environments.
- Isolation: Northflank Cloud uses microVMs for CPU sandboxes and gVisor for GPU sandboxes, with isolation enabled automatically.

...

- Security: Northflank is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant, with Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) supported under Enterprise contracts.

cto.new migrated its sandbox infrastructure to Northflank in a couple of days after scaling on EC2 metal instances caused large capacity and cost jumps. The team went on to run thousands of daily container deployments with API-driven provisioning and per-second billing.

Best for: Teams running thousands of concurrent AI agent sandboxes, multi-tenant code execution, and parallel workloads that need custom images, persistent files, or GPUs.

Pricing: $0.01667/vCPU-hour and $0.00833/GB-hour, with H100 GPU plans at $2.74/hour all-inclusive (CPU and RAM included). Railway does not currently offer GPU instances.

## How do Northflank and Railway compare on pricing and total cost of ownership?

Both use usage-based pricing, but their billing units and operational responsibilities differ. Prices were checked on 25 August 2026.

- Railway: Free is $0 with $1 of monthly resources, Hobby is $5, Pro is $20, and Enterprise is custom. The monthly plan amount counts toward usage. Standard rates are $10 per GB of RAM per month, $20 per vCPU per month, $0.15 per GB per month for volume storage, and $0.05 per GB for egress. Compute is metered by the minute.
- Northflank: The free Sandbox includes always-on compute, two services, one database, and two cron jobs. Pay-as-you-go is self-service, has no seat fees, and uses per-second billing. Northflank Cloud rates are $0.01667 per vCPU hour and $0.00833 per GB hour. Enterprise adds invoice-based billing, volume discounts, commitments, SSO, audit logs, HA/DR, on-premises deployment, 24/7 support, SLAs, and FDE onboarding. BYOC infrastructure is billed directly by the cloud provider, while Northflank charges disclosed platform rates of $0.01389 per vCPU hour, $0.00139 per GB hour, and $0.00278 per GB of GPU VRAM hour.
- Total cost of ownership: Both platforms reduce operational work through different models. Railway operates the infrastructure. Northflank abstracts Kubernetes while preserving infrastructure control. Northflank BYOC lets teams use cloud credits, commitments, spot capacity, node-pool autoscaling, workload scheduling, and custom resource plans. Compare infrastructure, data operations, traffic, support, and the engineering work each platform removes or leaves with your team.

## How do Northflank and Vercel compare on pricing and operational responsibility?

Vercel combines a platform fee, deploying seats, usage, and optional charges. Northflank separates managed-cloud consumption or BYOC platform fees from the customer's infrastructure bill. Prices were checked on 26 August 2026.

- Vercel: Hobby is free for personal, non-commercial use. Pro costs $20 per month, includes one deploying seat and $20 usage credit, and bills additional usage on demand. Extra deploying seats cost $20 per month; Viewer seats are free. Enterprise is custom-priced. Pro lists SAML SSO at $300 per month and a HIPAA BAA at $350 per month.
- Northflank: The free Sandbox includes always-on compute, two services, one database, and two cron jobs. Pay-as-you-go has no seat fees and bills per second. Northflank Cloud costs $0.01667 per vCPU-hour and $0.00833 per GB-hour, plus storage and networking. Enterprise adds invoice billing, volume discounts, annual commitments, 24/7 support, and SLAs. In BYOC, the cloud provider bills infrastructure directly while Northflank charges $0.01389 per vCPU-hour, $0.00139 per GB-hour, and $0.00278 per GB of GPU VRAM-hour. Direct billing preserves cloud credits, commitments, and negotiated rates.
- Total cost: Include seats, builds, requests, data transfer, storage, networking, previews, support, cloud-provider charges, minimum capacity, and retained engineering work. Vercel Fluid compute begins at $0.128 per active CPU-hour and $0.0106 per provisioned GB-hour in lower-cost US regions.

Northflank can reduce total cost for sustained and mixed workloads, such as services, jobs, databases, and GPU applications, through per-second pricing, no pay-as-you-go seat fees, and BYOC that preserves cloud commitments while supporting custom plans, spot nodes, autoscaling, and workload scheduling. Vercel may cost less for bursty web workloads because active CPU is not billed during I/O waits, although memory charges continue during the invocation.
